Hi all — answering Sam's questions and adding technical notes. See also attached updated arch diagram (redwood-private-arch-diagram.png).

1) Control plane/data egress: For the VPC-private deployment we offer two models:
   - Default: control plane endpoints (auth, billing telemetry) are routed to Redwood control plane over restricted outbound endpoints. No inference payload (raw prompts/responses) leaves the customer VPC; only encrypted metadata and lifecycle signals are sent.
   - Strict isolation (zero control-plane egress): we support an isolated mode where the control plane runs in your account (private control plane) or an on-prem agent proxies control-plane traffic through your jump host; in that mode no telemetry or prompt/token metadata is sent to Redwood-managed endpoints. This is the recommended path for PII-sensitive workflows.

2) Logging & retention: Audit logs and request logs can be configured to:
   - Retain for a configurable window (default 365 days, configurable down to 0).
   - Forward logs in near-real-time to a customer S3 bucket or to your SIEM via Kinesis/Firehose.
   - Support automated retention policies (we can set a 90-day purge policy scoped to user-identifiable fields).

3) KMS/HSM: Customer-managed keys (CMK) are supported. In VPC deployment we integrate with your KMS (AWS KMS or external Vault/HSM) so that model artifacts and cache encryption keys never leave your key domain. HSM-backed keys are supported for encryption operations.

Network boundary notes:
- Required outbound: if not running private control plane, minimal outbound endpoints for image/model pull and control-plane heartbeats (TLS to allowlisted domains) are required. We can provide exact FQDNs/IP ranges in the technical call.
- Egress controls: we support VPC endpoints and NAT-less architectures. For truly air-gapped installs we provide an on-prem bundle (no external egress).

Adding a couple of security/compliance clarifications: 

- PII handling: We recommend scoping ML inference for PII-sensitive datasets into the strict isolation/private control plane mode. Additionally, we support request-level redaction hooks and prefix-only caching to minimize retained context.

- Audit & retention: We can configure logs to mask or remove user-identifiable fields before retention or forwarding; this is done via a transform lambda prior to S3 delivery. We will provide an example transform during the technical deep-dive.

- Data residency: All storage for the private deployment (models, caches, logs) can be constrained to the customer's AWS region. For multi-region failover we support replication with customer approval.

- Compliance artifacts: attaching the security questionnaire with our answers (security-questionnaire-acme.xlsx). We can also provide SOC2 evidence on request under an NDA.

Let me know if you want specific retention configurations (we can set a 90-day policy scoped to identifiable logs for the pilot).

—Rishi
